title: Abeon Role DTO
description:
One role an organisation can assign. Returned by `GET /api/v1/auth/admin/roles` so an administrator can see what is assignable before assigning it.

**Roles are per organisation** (ADR-0016): two organisations both have an `admin`, and they are different rows with independently editable grants. The `name` is what a token carries and what `PUT /admin/users/{id}/roles` accepts, because the numeric id is internal, organisation-scoped, and would let a caller name a row belonging to somebody else's tenant.

`permissions` is here because an administrator choosing between `admin` and `member` is choosing what somebody can do, and a name alone does not say that. It is descriptive, never authoritative: a client that derived its own authorisation from this list would be deriving it from a response instead of from the token (ADR-0010).

name.description: Role name within this organisation, e.g. `admin`. This is the value a JWT's `roles` claim carries and the value the assignment endpoint accepts.

label.description: Human-readable name for a screen. Null falls back to `name`.

permissions.description: Grants this role confers, in ADR-0001's permission grammar. Descriptive only — see above.

system.description: True for the roles every organisation is seeded with (`owner`, `admin`, `member`). A screen may want to stop somebody deleting one; nothing in Auth deletes roles yet, so this is advisory.
